reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of auxiliary likelihood-based ABC is to replace intractable likelihoods with tractable auxiliary models that yield an auxiliary likelihood function. This allows for approximate Bayesian inference in complex state-space models where direct likelihood evaluation is impossible. The method uses a score-based distance metric to compare observed and simulated data, avoiding repeated optimization. Integrated likelihood dimension reduction further improves efficiency by reducing the dimensionality of the summary statistics used in ABC. These primitives enable GSI to perform Bayesian inference on latent team strengths in NFL models where exact likelihoods are unavailable. The method relies on the assumption that the auxiliary model is sufficiently rich to capture the essential features of the true model. In GSE, these primitives support real-time situational reasoning by modeling latent dynamics through state transitions and score-based approximations. The key failure modes include auxiliary model misspecification, poor score function construction, and numerical instability in integration steps.
